_doc: folk_tiers (FOLK-007, optional): ascending favor tiers [{min 1..100 strictly rising, name, line? with {name}, gift? {item, count 1..3}}]; the first time a generated villager reaches a tier the line posts and the gift is given (highest new tier only; Folk.new_tiers). folk_greetings.weather (WEATHER-006): optional {weather kind: [lines]} used instead of the warm line for warm villagers on such a day. folk_quarrels (FOLK-004, optional; Folk.monthly_quarrel): each month, with chance (0..1), two generated adult villagers of your current region (not your family) fall out if the region has no open quarrel: world flag quarrel_<region> {a, b, topic, until} for `days` (>= 1). topics: [{id, text with {a} and {b}}]. outcomes: mediate {favor_a, favor_b, alignment, check {attribute, target}, fail_favor} (fail_favor <= 0 goes to both on a failed check), side_a / side_b {favor_winner, favor_loser}, extort {stones, favor_a, favor_b, alignment}. Folk.settle applies one. FOLK-006: mark_days (>= 1) is how long the way you settled it is remembered (world flag quarrel_mark_<region> {choice, a, b, loser, until}): mediate = the pair stand together at the first one's haunt; side_a/side_b = the loser greets you coldly with a folk_greetings.shunned line; extort = a rumor with requires_quarrel_mark 'extort'. folk_companions (FOLK-005, optional; Folk.invite): a living generated adult cultivator (realm above mortal) of your region with favor >= min_favor can be asked "Come exploring with me" once per cooldown_days (whole numbers >= 0); in that day's next fight they strike `blows` (>= 1) times their attack alongside you; afterwards their favor changes by +favor_win (win) or -favor_loss (loss), and on a loss they may (injury_chance 0..1) suffer the injuries.json id `injury`. folk_visits (WORLD-007; C-277 tea_lines / tip_tea_lines: arrays of strings or {season, text}, each with {name} and optional {progress}, picked by day over the current season's pool; Folk.tea_line; Folk.visitor): on a clear or cloudy day a generated adult villager of your region with favor >= min_favor (and at least folk_tips.min_favor) whose last tea with you (CharacterData.folk_visit_day) was cooldown_days or more ago may drop by with probability chance per day (hash of day and region, no rng): they stand beside your Family Home, else beside the meditation spot nearest the spawn. Sharing tea gives tea_favor (>= 0, ignores chat_max_favor) and with tip_chance (0..1) a folk_tips tip that skips the tip cooldown. folk_gifts (FOLK-002): {min_favor, cooldown_days, gifts: [{item, count, weight, text with {villager}/{item}/{count}}]}: when a generated villager greets you with favor >= min_favor and cooldown_days have passed since their last gift (CharacterData.folk_gift_day), they hand over one gift picked by hash(npc id + day) weighted by weight. folk_greetings (WORLD-003): warm {min_favor, lines} and cool {max_favor, lines}: what a generated villager says in passing when your favor with them is at least min_favor / at most max_favor (min_favor > max_favor; lines non-empty, {player} is your name). C-274: an optional folk_greetings.celebration object maps a celebration type (wedding, full_month, funeral) to non-empty lines ({player}, {partner}, {child}) used instead of the warm/cool bands while that villager's celebration is open. celebrations news (and types.*.news) may be a string or a non-empty array of strings, picked by day % size. Folk.greeting picks one by hash of npc id and day. Courtship and marriage rules (Family system). adult_age: minimum age in years to court or marry. courtship: min_favor (favor with the NPC needed to court them), favor_gain (favor per courtship outing), charisma_step (each this many Charisma points above 10 adds +1 favor_gain, below 10 removes 1; minimum gain 1), days (time per outing). proposal: min_favor (needed to propose), max_realm_gap (major realms apart, either way), max_alignment_gap (alignment points apart; righteous and demonic clash), days. concubine_rank: the rank id that a proud NPC (npcs.json 'proud': true) or one of a higher major realm than the proposer refuses. genders: one entry per data/names.json gender: partner_genders (genders this character may court) and ranks (rank id -> {name, max, max_per_realm (optional; extra slots per major realm index of the proposer)}). dual_cultivation: qi_bonus (extra qi fraction for both partners cultivating together, e.g. 0.5 = +50%), realm_step (bonus multiplier per major realm the partner is above you, below lowers it), min_factor/max_factor (clamp of the partner factor = sqrt(partner root multiplier) * (1 + realm_step)^gap), favor_per_month (favor each living spouse gains per month of game time), favor_per_session (favor from cultivating together), max_favor (passive and session favor stop here). eligible_npcs (optional): generated courtship candidates kept in every region at session start and on load (Npcs.ensure_eligible): per_gender (unmarried adult generated NPCs of each data/names.json gender per region), age_min/age_max (years), proud_chance (0-1, chance a spawned NPC is proud and refuses concubinage), bloodline_chance (optional, 0-1, chance a spawned NPC carries a bloodline from data/bloodlines.json, weighted by rarity), realms_by_danger (list indexed by the region danger, clamped to the last entry; each entry is a list of realm ids to pick from). children (FAM-003, optional): carrier_gender (the partner who carries a pregnancy; a couple without exactly one cannot conceive and must adopt), conception_days (time spent per attempt), conception_chance (0..1 per attempt), pregnancy_days, max_mortal_carrier_age (a mortal carrier older than this cannot conceive; cultivators can), genius_chance (0..1, child gets a single high-purity root regardless of parents), genius_purity_min, mutation_chance (0..1, the element count shifts by one, and per parent element it may be replaced by a new element), purity_variance (+- on inherited purity), attribute_variance (+- on the parents' attribute average), cultivation_start_age (years before a child can cultivate). adoption (FAM-003b, optional; Adoption system): max_age (oldest child in years that can be adopted, below adult_age), days (time the adoption takes), alignment (alignment shift for taking in a child), favor (the child's starting favor with the adopter), take_surname (true = the child takes the adopter's surname), max_adopted (adopted children per character), foundling_donation (spirit stones asked by an orphanage/temple for a foundling), foundling_age_min/foundling_age_max (years; foundlings are newly generated children). npc_families (FAM-003d, optional; NpcFamilies system): off-screen NPC family life, simulated monthly: marriage_chance_per_year (0..1, chance an unmarried eligible generated NPC marries an unrelated eligible NPC of the same region; NPCs the player knows never do), attempt_chance_per_month (0..1, chance a married NPC couple tries for a child that month, then children.conception_chance applies), max_children (a mother stops at this many children), prune_dead_years (FAM-013b: generated NPCs dead this many years whom no living NPC lists as parent, child or spouse and whom the player knows nothing of (family, rival, grudge, gratitude, favor, clan) are removed from the saved world; 0 = never), population_cap (soft cap: no NPC conceptions or off-screen marriages while this many NPCs are alive; pregnancies under way and courtship candidates spawned at session start/load can still exceed it). acquaintance (FAM-002h, optional): small talk and gifts so NPCs without dialogue can be befriended up to courtship: chat_days (time per chat), chat_favor (favor per chat), charisma_step (each this many Charisma points above 10 adds +1 chat favor, below 10 removes 1; minimum 1), chat_max_favor (chatting stops raising favor here; NPCs with a dialogue file are talked to through it instead), gift_days (time per gift), gift_price_per_favor (an item's price per point of favor; price-0 items are refused), gift_max_per_item (favor cap per gift), gift_max_favor (gifts stop raising favor here; keep it below proposal.min_favor so marriage still needs courtship), gift_like_mult (GIFT-001, optional, >= 1, default 1: a gift matching the NPC's npcs.json `likes` is worth this many times as much, rounded up), gift_dislike_favor (optional, <= 0, default 0: favor change for a gift matching `dislikes`; the item is still taken, even at gift_max_favor), taste_hint_favor (optional, int 0..100, default 20: chatting with a named NPC who has `likes` at this favor or more mentions one thing they are fond of, once). training (FAM-004, optional): teach_days (time to teach your child a technique you know), teach_min_age (years), assignments (id -> {name, kind, stones_per_month, days, min_age}): monthly training the player assigns to a child and pays for in spirit stones each month; kind 'cultivate' = days of extra cultivation at the child's home qi density (once old enough to cultivate), 'profession' = days of profession xp in a profession picked when assigning, 'technique' = days practicing the child's least-practiced unmastered technique. clan (FAM-005, optional): min_realm (realm id needed to found a clan), found_cost (spirit stones), found_days, requires_abode (FAM-005c, optional bool: founding needs a claimed abode, which becomes the clan seat; claiming another abode later moves the seat), suffix (clan name = surname + suffix), ranks (ordered list, highest first; the first is the clan head: {id, name, names (optional, gender -> name, e.g. Matriarch), max (optional, members of that rank), min_realm (optional)}), family_rank (rank id living spouses and descendants join at), recruit_min_favor (favor an NPC needs to join as a retainer), recruit_cost (spirit stones), recruit_days. clan.heir (FAM-008): birth_rank_order (spousal ranks of the mother at birth, best first; empty string = adopted or unknown) decides the default heir among the head's living children (then eldest first); titles per gender (fallback: title) for the heir. The head may designate any living descendant who is a clan member; when a head dies, the heir succeeds (else the highest-ranked, then eldest, living member). sect_entry (FAM-009c, optional): NPCs can belong to sects (CharacterData.sect {id, rank}; rank = the highest sect rank whose min_realm they reach, rising as they break through; sect members cultivate with the sect's cultivation_bonus). min_age_years (youngest age a child can be sent to a sect), days (time it takes to send one), clan_youth_chance (0..1, chance each clan child of at least min_age_years joins a sect that would accept them when an NPC clan is founded). home (FAM-011): the Family Home in each region where the player's living spouses or children live (FamilyHome system). visit_days (time spent at home with the family there), visit_favor (favor each spouse and child at home gains per visit; spouses stop at dual_cultivation.max_favor, children at max_child_favor), max_child_favor, move_days (time to bring the household to this home: every living spouse and every child under adult_age living elsewhere moves here). mentorship (MENTOR-001, optional; Mentorship system): pointers and spar are blocks of whole numbers >= 0. pointers: min_favor (<= 100), same_sect_min_favor (optional, <= min_favor; the favor needed when the NPC is in the same sect as the player; also valid on spar), cooldown_days (per NPC), days (time taken), practice_days (days of practice xp for one unmastered technique), shared_multiplier (>= 1, applied when the NPC knows the same technique), lines (MENTOR-005, optional array of strings, each with {npc} and {tech}; Mentorship.pointer_line picks lines[day % size] so the master's words vary month to month; missing or empty = the plain "watches your ... points out a flaw" sentence). spar (SPAR-001): min_favor, cooldown_days, days, practice_days, win_favor, max_realm_gap. letters (LETTER-001, optional; Letters system): monthly_chance (0..1, chance each month that the living, non-family NPC you know best writes), min_favor (<= 100; only NPCs with at least this favor write), max_kept (letters remembered), visit_favor (extra favor from your next chat with someone who invited you), kinds: list of {id, weight (> 0), text (may use {name}, {region}), effects (optional shared effect keys), min_favor (optional), visit (optional bool: sets the world flag letter_visit_<npc>, consumed by the next chat)}. breakthrough_news (NEWS-001, optional; Family.breakthrough_news): on a successful major-realm breakthrough every living NPC with favor >= min_favor gains `favor` (capped at 100) and a sect member gains `sect_reputation` with their own sect; ints >= 0, absent = nothing happens. A letters.kinds[].deal {mult (0.5..1), days (>= 1)} (SHOP-001) gives a friend's price: buying in the writer's region costs mult times as much for that many days (CharacterData.shop_deals). A letters.kinds[].request {item, count, days, favor, effects} asks the player for items in person: giving them to that NPC before `days` pass earns `favor` and applies `effects` (LETTER-003). LETTER-002: family_chance (0..1) is rolled first each month: a living spouse or child (12+) in a sect, else a living parent, writes a kind with `from`: "family" (default "friend"; friend and family kinds never mix) whose optional `favor` (LETTER-006, int >= 0, family kinds only; a spouse or child writer gains that much favor, capped at dual_cultivation.max_favor / home.max_child_favor) and optional `relation` (spouse, child or parent) matches the writer; family writers need no favor. celebrations (WORLD-005, optional; Folk): when two generated NPCs of your current region marry off-screen, a celebration stays open for `days` (>= 1); attending costs `attend_days` (>= 1), gives each newly-wed `favor` (>= 0, capped at acquaintance.gift_max_favor) and you `alignment`; the first gift to either of them meanwhile is worth `gift_mult` (>= 1) times as much. folk_requests (FOLK-001, optional; Folk.monthly_request): each month, with monthly_chance (0..1), a living generated adult villager of your current region with favor >= min_favor (-100..100) and no open request asks for an item, stored as a letter request with source "folk" (give it in person within `days` (>= 1); at most max_open (>= 1) folk requests open at once). asks: list of {item (items.json id), count [min, max] (ints >= 1), favor (1..15, added to the villager's favor), stones [min, max] (ints >= 0, spirit stones paid), text (needs {villager}, {count} and {item}), regions (optional list of region ids), seasons (optional list of season ids)}. folk_tips (FOLK-003, optional; Folk.roll_tip): chatting with a generated villager whose favor is at least min_favor (below acquaintance.chat_max_favor, where small talk stops) may (chance 0..1, at most once per cooldown_days, one tip at a time) earn a tip: an item a gather place in your region (else one route away) yields this season; for `days` (1..60) days gathering in that region adds `bonus` (1..5) of it. lines: non-empty; each a string or {text, seasons (optional, spring/summer/autumn/winter), weather (optional kind: rain, fog...)}, the text needing {item}; a line whose seasons/weather do not match today is skipped; may use {villager}, {region}, {place_kind}. folk_greetings (WORLD-003): warm {min_favor, lines} and cool {max_favor, lines}: what a generated villager says in passing when your favor with them is at least min_favor / at most max_favor (min_favor > max_favor; lines non-empty, {player} is your name). folk_tiers.name: Friend
folk_tiers.line: {name} waves you over. "You keep turning up when I need a hand. Come by for tea any time." They press a parcel on you.

folk_tiers.name: Close friend
folk_tiers.line: {name} says quietly that you are one of the few people in the village they truly trust, and hands you a bundle of herbs.

folk_tiers.name: Sworn friend
folk_tiers.line: {name} takes both your hands. "Whatever comes, you have a home and a friend here." They give you a pill kept for exactly such a day.

celebrations.label: Attend the wedding
news: Word spreads of a wedding in {region}: {text}
Red paper hangs over a doorway in {region}: {text}
celebrations.attend_text: You join the wedding of {names}, drink to their happiness and dance until late.

full_month.label: Attend the full-month feast
news: Word spreads of a newborn in {region}: {text}
A baby's first cry is heard in {region}: {text}
Neighbours in {region} carry eggs and rice to a new cradle: {text}
full_month.attend_text: You raise a cup at the full-month feast of {names} and wish the baby a long, healthy life.

funeral.label: Pay your respects
news: White cloth hangs on a door in {region}: {text}
Incense burns in a quiet house in {region}: {text}
funeral.attend_text: You burn incense and pay your respects with {names}, sharing in their grief.

asks.text: {villager} asks if you could bring {count} {item}; their mother's cough is back.
{villager} is short of herbs for a tea and asks you for {count} {item}.
{villager} wants to mend a plough and would be glad of {count} {item}.
{villager} is stitching winter coats and asks you for {count} {item}.
{villager} quietly asks if you could spare {count} {item} for a sick relative.
{villager} is hosting a supper and asks if you could bring {count} {item} from the pond.
{villager} has heard you walk the forest paths and asks for {count} {item}.

topics.text: {a} and {b} are not speaking since a boundary stone was moved in the night.
{a} lent {b} an ox, and it came back lame.
{a} and {b} have fallen out over a broken betrothal between their families.
{b} says {a} never repaid a debt of rice, and {a} says it was repaid twice.

tea_lines: You share a pot of tea with {name} and talk about small things. ({progress})

tea_lines.text: {name} brews the first tea of spring, green and bitter, and you sit in the doorway watching the swallows return. ({progress})
{name} cuts a cold melon on the step and the tea goes lukewarm beside it; you talk until the heat breaks. ({progress})
{name} roasts chestnuts in the ashes and pours tea to wash them down, and you trade harvest talk. ({progress})
{name} pulls two stools to the brazier and the tea steams in the cold air while you talk of small things. ({progress})

tip_tea_lines: Over the second cup, {name} grows thoughtful and lets slip something worth knowing. ({progress})
{name} refills your cup and talks of the hills in a low voice, as if sharing a secret. ({progress})
You and {name} sit long over the tea, and a useful scrap of local lore comes out with the dregs. ({progress})

gifts.text: {villager} presses a bundle of herbs into your hands: +{count} {item}.
{villager} slips you something wrapped in cloth: +{count} {item}.
{villager} presses a small pill into your palm, saying it was kept for a friend: +{count} {item}.
{villager} insists you take a moon cake from their kitchen: +{count} {item}.
{villager} leaves a cured hide at your feet: +{count} {item}.

kinds.text: {name} sends a few kind words and a small gift of herbs.
{name} writes that their cultivation has taken another step forward.
{name} invites you to visit them in {region} when you can.
{name} writes stiffly: "I did not think you would come so far. Do not mistake this for friendship. Keep climbing; I intend to stand beside you at the top."
{name} recalls the lecture where you met and sends a note of the elder's comments, three lines on settling the breath before a breakthrough.
{name}, now an apprentice in {region}, writes that their master's furnace is cold and asks if you could spare a Qi Gathering Pill when you pass.
{name} writes from {region} that their mother has been bedridden since the rains. The village has no spirit herbs to spare; could you bring three when you pass?
{name} is to forge a first sword in {region} and cannot afford the iron. They ask, with some embarrassment, for two lumps of iron essence.
{name} must cross the mountains to {region} before winter and asks if you could lend a Swift Wind Talisman for the road.
{name} faces a sect trial in {region} and must present the pelts of beasts they have hunted. "Two Mist Wolf pelts would see me through," they write. "I will remember it."
{name} writes from {region}: a caravan has come in with surplus goods, and they have set aside a little something at a friend's price.
{name} is to be wed in {region} this season and begs you to come drink to the couple. A red paper envelope of luck-money is enclosed.
{name} writes in a shaking hand that an elder of their clan has passed. The letter asks for nothing; it only wants someone to know.
{name} sends a page of notes on a stance they have been turning over for months. "It may suit you better than it ever suited me," they write.
{name} writes from {region}: the sect's rules are strict, but they think of you at every lamp-lighting.
{name} writes from {region} to ask how you would settle a doubt in their practice. Answering takes only a few lines, and you feel steadier for it.
{name} writes that they worry about you on the road, and sends dried herbs from the garden.
{name} sends word that the road to {region} is quiet this month, along with a pouch of mountain tea to steady the mind.

lines: {villager} leans in: "After the last rain the {place_kind} in {region} is thick with {item}. Go before the others hear."
{villager} lowers their voice: "If you want {item}, try the {place_kind} in {region} this week."
"I shouldn't tell anyone," says {villager}, "but the {place_kind} in {region} is rich in {item} right now."
{villager} presses your hand: "Friend, look for {item} at the {place_kind} in {region}. You will not be sorry."

lines.text: {villager} grins: "The thaw woke the {place_kind} in {region}. {item} is coming up before anyone else has looked."
{villager} wipes their brow: "Hot as it is, the shade at the {place_kind} in {region} keeps {item} fat. Go at dawn."
{villager} nods at the stubble: "Harvest leaves {item} lying about the {place_kind} in {region}. Gather before the frost."
{villager} blows on their hands: "Everyone sits by the brazier, so the {place_kind} in {region} is yours. {item} keeps under the frost."
{villager} shakes out a wet cloak: "With this rain the {place_kind} in {region} must be full of {item}. Take a hat."
{villager} peers into the white: "Fog sits on the {place_kind} in {region}, and {item} hides in it. Go slowly."
{villager} ducks in from the downpour: "Nobody is out in this storm, so the {place_kind} in {region} is yours. {item} washes loose after thunder."
{villager} looks up at the black sky: "After a storm like this, the {place_kind} in {region} gives up {item}. Wait for the thunder to pass."
{villager} bars the shutter: "When the lightning stops, try the {place_kind} in {region}. {item} is thrown up after a storm like this."

storm: {player}! Out in this? Come under the eaves, the thunder is walking the hills.
Good day, {player}. Bar your door tonight; the sky is angry.
{player}, mind the lightning. Friends are scarcer than rain.

wedding: {player}! Come to the wedding feast, {partner} and I have wine enough for all.
Good day, {player}. Such a happy day, the whole lane is dancing.
{player}, stay for the toasts, {partner} will pour. Luck is better shared.
full_month: {player}, have you seen the baby? Come, have a red egg.
Welcome, {player}. We are celebrating the little one's full month.
Good day, {player}. Wish {child} a long and healthy life.
funeral: {player}. Thank you for coming; we have burned incense all morning.
Quietly now, {player}. Our house is in mourning.
Good day, {player}. Forgive me, my mind is on the funeral.

lines: {player}! Come by later, I owe you thanks for your help.
Good day, {player}. Take a pear from my basket, please.
There you are, {player}. Your cultivation shows; the whole village is proud.
{player}, you are always welcome at my door.
Ah, {player}! I told my neighbours how you helped me.
Walk in peace, {player}. The village remembers kindness.

shunned: {player}. You took their side. I remember.
They look through you as if you were not there.
"Go and sit with your friends," they say, and turn away.

lines: They see you coming and turn away without a word.
They mutter something under their breath as you pass.
"You again," they say, and hurry off.
They pull their door shut as you near.
{npc} watches your {tech} and points out a flaw.
{npc} taps your elbow mid-strike: your {tech} leaks its force there.
Watching your {tech}, {npc} says nothing for a long while, then shows you where your breath breaks.
{npc} shifts your stance a finger's width, and your {tech} suddenly sits steady.
"Your intent runs ahead of your hands," says {npc}, and slows your {tech} until the two meet.
{npc} presses a thumb to your wrist: the qi in your {tech} pools where it should flow.
{npc} walks you through your {tech} once, breathing with you, and names the meridian that stalls.
"Again, but empty your mind," says {npc}. Your {tech} lands cleaner for it.
{npc} sweeps your back foot aside and smiles: your {tech} has no root, and now you feel why.
{npc} circles you in silence, then corrects the turn of your waist in {tech}.
